newsitem.title: UK: Conoco, Reading & Bates in deep water drill venture.
newsitem.headline: Conoco, Reading & Bates in deep water drill venture.

text.p: Dupont's energy subsidiary Conoco said on Thursday it has formed a 50/50 joint venture with Reading & Bates to carry out a $400 million drilling programme initially centred on the Gulf of Mexico.
The new company has commissioned construction of a $200 million drillship capable of drilling in water up to 10,000 feet deep from Korea's Samsung Heavy Industries, Conoco said.
The double-hulled vessel, which will be able to perform extended well tests and includes crude oil storage and offloading capacity, is expected to be delivered in 1998.

"Having a drillship solely dedicated to Conoco's deep water operations fits our strategy of resuming a leadership role in exploring the deep waters of the region," said Conoco president and chief executive Archie Dunham.
Conoco's marine department will assist in the design of the vessel and oversee construction. Reading & Bates will provide drilling services to the new venture.

"We are very pleased to enter into this significant agreement with Conoco which will result in the long-term development of a new generation deep water drilling vessel," said Reading & Bates chairman Paul Loyd.
Conoco produces 41,000 barrels per day of oil from the Gulf of Mexico, where it has leases on 1.2 million acres.
Other areas of deep water exploration include offshore Norway and Britain, the Niger Delta and offshore New Zealand.

In simultaneous announcements in London and the U.S., Conoco's executive vice president for exploration and production Rob McKee said, "This is the most advanced drillship our industry has ever seen."
"Advanced technology such as this will give Conoco the ability to extend its exploratory efforts beyond traditional offshore shelf areas so that deeper fields can be developed economically."
The new company will carry out a five year drilling programme for Conoco, beginning in 60 blocks recently acquired in the Gulf of Mexico which range in water depth between from 2,000 to 9,000 feet.
